title_en: Hollywood Was Cooked Before AI, and Now It's Only Getting Worse
title_zh: AI 之前好莱坞就已完蛋，如今只会更糟——对话 LA Material 创意总监 Hayes Davenport
subtitle_zh: 编剧 Hayes Davenport 谈洛杉矶拍摄日腰斩、迷你编剧室、AI 冲击与创意经济的连锁反应。
summary_zh: 本期 Odd Lots 在 Hollywood 的 Vermont Theater 现场录制，Tracy Alloway 与 Joe Weisenthal 对话编剧、LA Material 创意总监、播客 Hollywood Handbook 联合主持人 Hayes Davenport（曾参与 Eastbound and Down、Family Guy），剖析给好莱坞写剧本这门生意的衰落。Davenport 用拍摄日（shoot days）这一行业指标串起全篇：LA 拍摄日在 2016 年见顶约 40,000 个，2019 年回落至约 37,000，经历疫情积压、2022 年短暂回到 37,000，随后罢工与需求萎缩令其一路跌破 20,000——只剩峰值的一半，业内曾流行的口号是熬到 25 年（survive till 25）。他解释 2016 到 2019 的下滑源于流媒体（Netflix、Amazon）增长与传统有线电视收缩的此消彼长，失业编剧转向播客或糊口活儿（survival jobs），而摄影棚地产却在需求见顶时才建成。他还谈及 AI 对化妆、发型、布景、灯光助理（grips）等一线制作岗位的连锁冲击，以及名流文化从 Trocadero 转向农夫市集的变迁。是一集关于创意经济萎缩的现场深谈。

turns.en: Is everyone cooked? I.

turns.en: if you want to do the numbers, I can talk about like shoot days in LA. The numbers that we look at are, are, are shoot days. Like that's the metric. And that's for reality, for commercials, that's for everything, right? Shoot days in LA, uh, hit a high in 2016, about 40,000 shoot days. And from there it sort of leveled out to around 37,000 by 2019. Okay. Pandemic hits the shoot days collapse, obviously. There's a backlog. And then in 2021, they sort of skyrocket again. 2022, we're back to 2019 numbers, around 37,000. The next year, 2023, the strikes hit. Shoot days fall again to 25,000. The next year, people are sort of hoping for a recovery. They end up at 23,000. Shoot days fall again. The mantra I think a lot of people heard in the city was survive till 25. That was like a phrase in the entertainment industry here. And instead, shoot days fell again to under 20,000. So that is half of what it was in 2016. Maybe. Maybe.
turns.zh: 如果要说数据的话，我可以讲讲洛杉矶的拍摄日（shoot days）。我们看的指标就是拍摄日，就是这个口径。这涵盖真人秀、广告，涵盖所有东西，对吧？洛杉矶的拍摄日在 2016 年达到高峰，大约 40,000 个拍摄日。之后大致回落到 2019 年的 37,000 左右。好。疫情来了，拍摄日显然崩了。然后出现了积压。到 2021 年又猛地飙升。2022 年，我们回到 2019 年的水平，大约 37,000。第二年，2023 年，罢工来了。拍摄日再次跌到 25,000。再下一年，大家还盼着复苏，结果只有 23,000。拍摄日又跌了。我觉得当时城里很多人听到的口号就是'熬到 25 年'（survive till 25）。这在本地娱乐行业是一句流行语。可结果呢，拍摄日又跌到了 20,000 以下。也就是说只有 2016 年的一半。也许吧，也许吧。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: Actually, we'll talk about the impact of COVID and the strike, and I guess we're unfortunately going to have to talk about AI. Is there a theory for the 2016 to 2019 decline? If we started there, is there a conventional wisdom about what happened in those three years?
turns.zh: 其实我们待会儿会聊新冠和罢工的影响，而且很遗憾我们恐怕还得聊聊 AI。对于 2016 到 2019 年的下滑，有没有什么解释？如果从那里说起，关于那三年到底发生了什么，业内有没有一种公认的说法？

turns.en: I think you saw it. An increase, obviously, in the streaming economy. There were more shows on Netflix and Amazon. Entire new networks being built. I remember when House of Cards started when I was first a writer and we called it a web series. We didn't really know what it was. And at the same time, a decline in the number of network productions and cable. Cable was shrinking around the same time. So that's how you get to like. like a leveling out between 40,000 and 37,000. My first couple jobs were comedy central shows. Uh, comedy central does not really do new shows anymore. Uh, and so that like you, you, you can see just from the options that are sent you as a writer, uh, what is growing in terms of streaming and what is sort of falling away, which was cable.
turns.zh: 我觉得你能看到，流媒体经济显然在增长。Netflix 和 Amazon 上的剧集更多了，全新的电视网在不断建立。我记得 House of Cards 刚出的时候，那还是我刚开始当编剧，我们把它叫做'网络剧'（web series），当时我们也不太清楚它到底算什么。与此同时，传统电视网的制作数量和有线电视在下滑，有线电视那阵子也在萎缩。所以你就得到了在 40,000 和 37,000 之间趋于平稳的这个结果。我最早的几份工作是 Comedy Central 的节目。Comedy Central 现在基本不再做新节目了。所以，仅仅从一个编剧能收到的那些活儿选项，你就能看出流媒体这块在增长，而什么在消退——那就是有线电视。

turns.en: So what happens to all the unemployed writers? Do they, I guess they all start podcasts.
turns.zh: 那那些失业的编剧都去哪儿了？他们是不是……我猜都去做播客了。

turns.en: Yeah, that's that has been sort of a safe harbor for a lot of us. Some people move like an interesting thing happened is the the membership in the Writers Guild grew a lot in the late 2010s. OK, because of people moving out, because everyone who had worked on a cable show was still a member of the Writers Guild and many more new shows were starting that were bringing new people into the business. and I think it is a lot of the newcomers that then, as production has been cut in half since then, that are not seeing the same opportunities. So, I mean, I know people who have moved home, for sure, and have taken on, you know, I work with a news outlet now, we did a piece about people that have taken on different survival jobs around the city, so it varies, but yeah, people are struggling, for sure.
turns.zh: 对，做播客对我们很多人来说算是个避风港。有些人搬走了。有件有意思的事是，2010 年代后期编剧工会（Writers Guild）的会员数量增长了很多。好，因为有人搬走，也因为凡是做过有线电视剧集的人都还是工会会员，而且当时有更多新剧在启动，把新人带进这一行。我觉得正是那些新人，在后来制作量被砍掉一半之后，没能获得同样的机会。所以，我是说，我确实认识一些搬回老家的人，也去做了各种……你知道，我现在在一家新闻机构工作，我们做过一期报道，讲人们在这座城市里干各种'糊口活儿'（survival jobs），情况各不相同，但没错，大家确实过得很艰难。

turns.en: I joked about it, you know, And we're going to talk more about it later, but, you know, there's this sort of the influencer creator world.
turns.zh: 我刚才是开玩笑说的，不过我们待会儿会多聊聊，就是那个网红创作者（influencer creator）的世界。

turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.zh: 还有'经济'。好。行业指的是那些制片厂、电视网，也就是传统好莱坞。但网红网络绝对也是经济的一部分。

turns.en: It is... Taking money from subscribers around the world and like putting it into the local economy. And so it's really, really important. And I look at things like I get jealous of places like New York because what New York feels to me now as a social media user is a place where you just walk down the street and people ask you what you're listening to or where you get your confidence from. Or what song is this? We don't have that here. I've never been asked that here.
turns.zh: 它就是……把全世界订阅者的钱拿过来，投入本地经济。所以这真的非常非常重要。我会关注这些事，我有点嫉妒纽约这样的地方，因为作为一个社交媒体用户，纽约现在给我的感觉是：你走在街上，就会有人问你在听什么、你的自信从哪儿来的，或者'这是什么歌？'。我们这儿没有这种氛围，我在洛杉矶从没被人这么问过。

turns.en: I'm actually really paranoid about being accosted by one of those people who was like, what do you pay in rent?
turns.zh: 我其实特别怕被那种人搭讪，上来就问我：'你房租付多少？'

turns.en: Can I come home with you? Can I come see where you live?
turns.zh: '我能跟你回家吗？我能去看看你住哪儿吗？'

turns.en: It seems like you have.
turns.zh: 看样子你还真……

turns.en: To say yes.
turns.zh: 得答应他们。

turns.en: There's a lot of that. You don't have to say yes. A lot of people do. I live in fear of just one of those random... What if.
turns.zh: 这种事很多。你不一定要答应。但很多人都答应了。我就一直提心吊胆，怕碰到那种随便什么人……万一呢。

turns.en: They showed my clip of me saying no? Yeah.
turns.zh: 他们播了我拒绝的那段片段？是啊。

turns.en: No, I know. What do you do?
turns.zh: 不，我知道。你能怎么办？

turns.en: We need some protocol for, like, it's like, I'm opting out.

turns.zh: 对。

turns.en: The no comment.

turns.en: Like, we don't have that. Like, I kind of wish we did. But, like, honestly, it seems so... I really do. It seems so stupid. But, like, it tells a story about New York that is exporting it to the rest of the country. Interesting. Which is, like, what we have had in L.A., we sort of had a... We had that corner for decades.
turns.zh: 就是，我们没有那种东西。我倒希望我们有。但说实话，这事儿看起来太……我真的这么觉得，看起来很蠢。但它讲出了一个关于纽约的故事，纽约正在把它输出到全国其他地方。有意思。也就是说，我们在洛杉矶一直拥有的东西，我们算是……几十年来我们一直独占着那个角落。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: Like, every... movie and show you'd see the venice boardwalk some like a girl on rollerblades like like we were we were exporting right yeah and we're not doing that in the same way when it comes to social media we are on some things people know about erwan smoothies in central europe because of our influencer economy yeah uh but it's uh we don't own it yeah the same way as we did We.
turns.zh: 就是，每部……电影和剧里你都能看到 Venice 海滨步道，某个踩轮滑的女孩，就像我们在向外输出一样，对吧，是的。可在社交媒体这块，我们已经不再以同样的方式输出了。有些东西我们确实做到了——比如中欧的人知道 Erewhon 的果昔，就是靠我们的网红经济，是的。但这……我们不再像过去那样主导它了，我们……

turns.zh: 顺便说一句，我们试着请 Erewhon 的 CEO 上这个节目，结果据说他们完全不接受媒体采访，可却有这种了不起的……

turns.en: Oh, there's so many people doing media for them.
turns.zh: 哦，有那么多人替他们做媒体传播。

turns.en: Oh, yeah, there we go.
turns.zh: 哦对，就是这么回事。

turns.en: It's part of it, yeah.
turns.zh: 这也是其中一部分，是的。

turns.en: All right, since we're talking about, I guess, geographical comparisons, when it comes to production, can you explain, like, why is L.A.
turns.zh: 好，既然我们在聊，我猜是地理上的比较，就制作而言，你能解释一下，为什么洛杉矶

turns.en: Actually losing out? Because I see.
turns.zh: 反而在输？因为我看到

turns.en: Headlines like Netflix is building a $ 1 billion studio in New Jersey, and no offense to New Jerseyans, but, you know, we come to L.A., Seems pretty nice.
turns.zh: 这样的头条：Netflix 要在新泽西建一座 10 亿美元的制片厂。无意冒犯新泽西人，但是，你知道，我们来到洛杉矶，觉得这儿挺不错的。

turns.en: Yeah, that's a big one for sure. It's been a bit of a race to the bottom across the country. And I have worked on shows. So you mentioned Eastbound and Down. We were in North Carolina until they got rid of their tax break there. The governor sort of single-handedly ended it. And then we just ran across the border to South Carolina for the last... For their next show that they did, it was a show called Vice Principals, the eastbound team. We shot that in South Carolina. And they've kept doing Righteous Gemstones there. It followed the tax break. Great show. I ran a show. We did a pilot for TBS. It was in Vancouver. A lot of my friends are shooting in Vancouver now. And what is kind of most surprising to me, game shows. Like, if you see a Fox game show... Or a Fox studio comedy, like a single cam or a multi-cam comedy. You're in Dublin. You are watching a show that is filmed in Dublin.
turns.zh: 对，那绝对是个大因素。全国范围内这有点像一场'逐底竞争'（race to the bottom）。我自己也参与过一些剧。你提到 Eastbound and Down，我们当时在北卡罗来纳州拍，直到他们取消了那里的税收优惠，州长几乎是凭一己之力把它终止了。然后我们就直接跨过州界去了南卡罗来纳州，为了最后……他们做的下一部剧，叫 Vice Principals，就是 Eastbound 那个团队，我们在南卡罗来纳拍的。他们一直在那儿拍 Righteous Gemstones，就是跟着税收优惠走。很棒的一部剧。我还主创过一部剧，我们给 TBS 拍了个试播集（pilot），是在温哥华。我很多朋友现在都在温哥华拍戏。而最让我意外的是游戏竞赛节目（game shows）。比如你看到一档 Fox 的游戏节目，或者一部 Fox 制片厂的情景喜剧，单镜或多镜喜剧，那你其实是在都柏林——你看的是一档在都柏林拍摄的节目。

turns.en: So they're flying out Rob Lowe and an American game show contestant cast. I didn't know that. to that you know you used to like get you'd go to universal studios and get to just like be.

turns.zh: 那是税收的原因，还是单纯便宜很多？

turns.en: It's a tax and labor thing yeah wow um and and meanwhile we have tons of studio space here so you talk about that 2016 peak yeah in shoot days that's when a lot of studio space started to get financed and so right down the street from here there a giant complex right on the on the santa monica and the 101 that you saw starting to get built around like 2019 or so that's when it got financed there was a gigantic hole in the ground for for a really long time and now it is done and And the demand is not exactly what it was. turns.zh: 最好是由一整间编剧室来写？

turns.en: I've always wanted to ask this question.
turns.zh: 我一直想问这个问题。

turns.en: Why isn't it not just someone who's like a play or a screenplay or whatever where you have a single writer?
turns.zh: 为什么不像戏剧或者电影剧本那样，就一个编剧单独搞定？

turns.en: Why doesn't that work in TV?
turns.zh: 为什么这种方式在电视剧里行不通？

turns.en: I mean, that economy is, sorry, you accidentally did ask a question about the current TV economy because it is shifting to, you know, what people talk about is like the Mike White model. Mike White goes and does the White Lotus by himself. He writes that show. Um, I'm pretty sure I like DTF St. Louis, I think is like done the same way. A lot of prestige shows are kind of written by one, uh, one, one person, the studios like that. God, it is cheaper. Yeah.
turns.zh: 我是说，那个经济……抱歉，你其实不小心问到了一个关于当下电视剧经济的问题，因为它正在转向——大家常说的那个'Mike White 模式'。Mike White 自己一个人做 The White Lotus，那部剧是他一个人写的。我挺确定，像 DTF St. Louis 我觉得也是用同样的方式做的。很多高口碑剧集（prestige shows）差不多就是一个人写的，制片厂喜欢这样，天哪，这样更便宜。是的。

turns.en: Uh, but historically it wasn't like that.
turns.zh: 呃，但历史上并不是这样的。

turns.en: Oh yeah, totally. And when it comes to like, I worked on a show called great news, which was kind of in the 30 rock family where the joke density family guys, the same way family guy had 30 writers when I was there. That does not exist anymore and never, ever will again.
turns.zh: 哦对，完全是。就……我参与过一部叫 Great News 的剧，它算是 30 Rock 那一挂的，那种笑话密度，Family Guy 也一样——我在的时候 Family Guy 有 30 个编剧。那种情况现在已经不存在了，而且永远、永远都不会再有了。

turns.en: Wait, so this is the mini room phenomenon, right? People call these mini rooms where you have smaller teams of writers. And everyone seems to hate them, even though, you know, we live in New York. Mini rooms don't sound terrible. We're used to them.
turns.zh: 等等，所以这就是所谓'迷你编剧室'（mini room）现象，对吧？大家管这些叫迷你编剧室，就是编剧团队更小。似乎所有人都讨厌它，不过你知道，我们住在纽约，迷你编剧室听起来也没那么糟，我们习惯了。

turns.en: But I guess in Hollywood.
turns.zh: 但我猜在好莱坞……

turns.en: What a mini room used to mean to me on Family Guy. was a room of seven writers that would break off to go write one joke. Huh. Wow. And now that is a big room. Seven writers is like a big room for a show. The last show I helped out with was the two creators of the show had a budget to have one person come in and just outline the season for a couple weeks. And then they went and wrote it themselves. So the rooms are getting smaller and smaller. Part of it is a result of the strikes where If you have a room now, it has to be of a certain size and for a certain number of weeks.
turns.zh: 以前在 Family Guy，'迷你编剧室'对我来说，是指七个编剧分出去专门写一个笑话。哈。哇。而现在，那已经算大编剧室了。七个编剧对一部剧来说已经算大团队了。我最近帮忙的那部剧，两位主创的预算只够请一个人进来，花几周时间把整季的大纲列出来，然后他们自己再去写。所以编剧室越来越小。部分原因是罢工的结果：现在你要是开一个编剧室，它必须达到一定规模、持续一定的周数。

turns.en: Oh.
turns.zh: 哦。

turns.en: So if they trigger a writer's room, then it is required to be a certain size, and that has changed the calculus a little bit. But I'll say, with a show like Great News, with a show like Family Guy, it is almost impossible to come up with a show like, to write a show like that as one person. Yeah. And you have a spot in the script for a joke, and people are just, like, pitching that. in a room setting, and you see what gets a laugh.
turns.zh: 所以如果他们要启动一个编剧室，那它就必须达到规定规模，这在一定程度上改变了他们的盘算。但我得说，像 Great News、像 Family Guy 这样的剧，一个人几乎不可能构思出、写出这样一部剧。是的。剧本里有个地方需要放一个笑话，大家就在编剧室的环境里不停地抛点子，看哪个能逗笑大家。

turns.en: Wow.
turns.zh: 哇。

turns.en: On Family Guy, you would have to be able to do the accents of the different, you would have to be able to do the voices.
turns.zh: 在 Family Guy，你得会模仿不同角色的口音，你得会配那些角色的声音。

turns.en: So that the people in the room could understand how the joke would land.
turns.zh: 好让编剧室里的人明白这个笑话会是什么效果。

turns.en: If you can't do Lois, your joke will not get in.
turns.zh: 如果你不会配 Lois 的声音，你的笑话就进不去。

turns.en: Can you do Lois?
turns.zh: 你会配 Lois 吗？

turns.en: No.
turns.zh: 不会。

turns.en: It's a bizarre, it makes no sense.
turns.zh: 这很荒唐，毫无道理。

turns.en: Wait, which character did you write the most jokes for, looking back?
turns.zh: 等等，回头看，你给哪个角色写的笑话最多？

turns.en: The hardest voice to do was Chris. Seth Green is like, it's amazing what he can do. I would say probably Peter. Brian is hard. Brian is subtle. But Peter, you know, Peter's very easy and fun to write for.
turns.zh: 最难配的声音是 Chris。Seth Green 简直……他能做到的东西太惊人了。要我说，写得最多的可能是 Peter。Brian 很难，Brian 很微妙。但 Peter，你知道，Peter 写起来又轻松又有意思。

turns.en: It was interesting.
turns.zh: 这很有意思。

turns.en: Like family guy memes are like the lingua franca of the internet. Like there's like more than any, like way more than many other shows.
turns.zh: 就是 Family Guy 的表情包（memes）几乎是互联网的通用语（lingua franca）。它比任何……比很多其他剧都要多得多。

turns.en: There are so many, something.
turns.zh: 有太多那种……什么来着。

turns.en: About that show is just like designed for like memetics and templates and you like re, you know, put out some other caption.
turns.zh: 那部剧就像是专门为表情包和模板设计的，你可以，你知道，重新配上一句别的说明文字。

turns.en: But that's a threat to the new TV shows as well. The fact that, we are still competing against Family Guy every time we do a new show. That did not used to be the case. The entire library is competition, not just what's on the other network at the same time.
turns.zh: 但这对新剧也是一种威胁。事实是，我们每次做一部新剧，都还在跟 Family Guy 竞争。以前并不是这样。整个片库（library）都是竞争对手，而不只是同一时段别的电视网在播的东西。

turns.en: This is something that I wanted to ask you, but in the age of AI and now that there's so much existing content out there, do you get the sense that libraries are becoming more.
turns.zh: 这是我一直想问你的：在 AI 时代，而且现在市面上有这么多既有内容，你会不会觉得片库正变得更……

turns.en: Or less valuable? Because you could kind of see it going either way, right?
turns.zh: 更有价值，还是更没价值？因为这事儿往哪个方向走都说得通，对吧？

turns.en: Yeah, I mean, individual shows are definitely still really valuable. Family Guy, The Office, like those will still command like a big price. But yeah, I think in the same way that new shows are competing against the old ones, the old ones are competing against each other. And some big chunks of the library, I think, are also becoming less and less valuable as well.
turns.zh: 是的，我是说，单独的剧集肯定仍然非常有价值。Family Guy、The Office，这些仍然能卖出高价。但没错，我觉得就像新剧在跟老剧竞争一样，老剧之间也在互相竞争。而片库里一些很大的板块，我认为也正变得越来越不值钱。

turns.en: Hmm. As of 2026, what are the norms about essentially the use.
turns.zh: 嗯。截至 2026 年，关于……本质上就是使用

turns.en: Of AI within creation?
turns.zh: AI 来进行创作，现在的常态是怎样的？

turns.en: You know, I don't speak for the whole city. I think this is one of the least AI-friendly cities in the world. The country, I would guess. When it comes to generative AI, I think it's pretty widely used, like everyone else, as a search engine. Yeah, sure, yeah. The way everyone uses it. There is still a lot of stigma on my. Podcasts we had a guest on recently who had been involved in a project that had one piece of it that had apparently been done with some AI. And there was like a pushback about that just because right now it is such a threat. Yeah. uh to jobs to like the the below the line economy in the city we call it like uh is uh but what is what does that mean below the line they're like anyone who works on the production side oh i see yeah um and so hair and makeup uh people like set design grips things like that like That is sort of on an immediate precipice when it comes to AI. And when it comes to the local economy of LA, that is a really huge issue. That level of job loss is a huge issue. I worked in City Hall for a while. It has huge ripple effects on the rest of the economy. I think people here have a sense of that, and it has... it has made it a line that a lot of people say you just do not cross when it comes to productions. Yeah.
turns.zh: 你知道，我不能代表整座城说话。我觉得这是全世界对 AI 最不友好的城市之一，我猜在全国也是。说到生成式 AI（generative AI），我认为它用得很普遍，就跟其他人一样，当搜索引擎用。是的，当然，就是大家用它的那种方式。但在我的……还是有很多污名。我们播客最近请了一位嘉宾，他参与过一个项目，其中一个环节显然是用 AI 做的，结果就招来了反弹，只因为眼下 AI 是个巨大的威胁。是的，呃，对工作岗位，对城里我们所说的'线下'（below the line）经济——那是什么意思？'线下'就是所有在制作一线干活的人，哦，懂了，是的——所以像化妆师、发型师、布景设计、灯光助理（grips）这类人，在 AI 面前可以说是命悬一线。而对洛杉矶本地经济来说，这是个非常大的问题，那种程度的失业是个大问题。我在市政厅（City Hall）工作过一段时间，它对经济的其他部分有巨大的连锁反应。我觉得这里的人对此有切身体会，这也让它成了一条红线，很多人说，在制作上你就是绝对不能越过这条线。是的。

turns.en: So I read that the new WGA contract, the writers union contract has some AI protection guardrails in it.
turns.zh: 我看到新的 WGA 合同，也就是编剧工会的合同，里面有一些针对 AI 的保护性护栏条款。

turns.en: How effective would you expect those to be?
turns.zh: 你觉得这些条款会有多有效？

turns.en: And I guess how long until the studios just find workarounds for those?
turns.zh: 还有，我猜，制片厂要多久才能找到绕过这些条款的办法？

turns.en: I have not heard of a show that has been written by AI yet. So at LA material, we did a story about how, um, Short stories are very popular IP now and not like Harper's type short stories, like things that are posted on Reddit or in some cases like totally unpublished short stories by anonymous writers. Were those written by AI? It's really hard to tell. But when it comes to the work that writers are doing, obviously you can't police what people do in their own homes.
turns.zh: 我还没听说过有哪部剧是 AI 写的。在 LA Material，我们做过一期报道，讲的是……短篇小说现在是非常抢手的 IP，而且不是 Harper's 那种短篇小说，是发在 Reddit 上的东西，有些甚至是匿名作者从未发表过的短篇小说。那些是 AI 写的吗？真的很难说。但就编剧们正在做的工作而言，显然你没法监管别人在自己家里干什么。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: But it has not come for writers' rooms in the same way. Studios aren't saying, like, we got this. We're just going to have AI take care of this so far.
turns.zh: 但 AI 还没有以同样的方式杀进编剧室。制片厂并没有说'这个我们搞定了，就交给 AI 来处理吧'，到目前为止还没有。

turns.en: Do they want to? Like, do you feel it?
turns.zh: 他们想这么干吗？就是，你能感觉到吗？

turns.en: Like, either the studio's hoping that maybe there's some model.
turns.zh: 就是说，要么制片厂在盼着也许有某个模型……

turns.en: None of them are funny.
turns.zh: 它们没一个好笑的。

turns.en: Yet, but are they, like, you know, hoping that there could be a model that can produce jokes? Or do you see the presence of, like, startups coming to pitch studios and say, like, this thing they can play, like, are there people banging at the gate trying to like break through? And I guess like, you know, break that eventually hoping that the dam will break on this.
turns.zh: 目前还没有，但他们是……你知道，在盼着能有一个可以产出笑话的模型吗？还是说你能看到一些初创公司跑来向制片厂推销，说'这东西他们能用'，就是有人在敲门、试图突破？我猜，你知道，他们最终是在盼着这道堤坝会决口。

turns.en: You know, the, the genre that is the most alive in Hollywood right now is horror.
turns.zh: 你知道，眼下好莱坞最有生命力的类型片是恐怖片。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: And great horror movies.
turns.zh: 而且是优秀的恐怖片。

turns.en: They're great. And so many people, you know, like Zach Kreger used to be on team comedy and We lost him to Tim Hortons. Jordan Peele also was a comedy guy. This is where a lot of great filmmakers are moving into.
turns.zh: 它们很棒。而且这么多人，你知道，像 Zach Kreger 以前是喜剧阵营的，我们把他输给了 Tim Hortons。Jordan Peele 以前也是搞喜剧的。这正是很多优秀电影人正在转入的领域。

turns.en: Why?
turns.zh: 为什么？

turns.en: What is it about horror that is having this moment?
turns.zh: 恐怖片到底是有什么特别之处，让它正迎来这个高光时刻？

turns.en: You can make a mid-budget movie that is commercially viable, that a studio will put out because they know it will make more money. It started with studios like Blumhouse that made Paranormal Activity for whatever, $ 20, and it makes millions. uh, comedy does not have the same upside potential. It doesn't have the same, uh, perceived theater going potential right now. So that's like to answer your question, like comedy is hardest for AI to do. Yeah. Uh, but it can do other genres more easily. It can do outlines right now.
turns.zh: 你可以拍一部中等预算、商业上可行的电影，制片厂愿意发行，因为他们知道它能赚更多钱。这是从 Blumhouse 这样的制片厂开始的，他们用大概……20 美元拍了 Paranormal Activity，结果赚了几百万。呃，喜剧没有同样的上行潜力，眼下它没有同样的、被看好的吸引观众进影院的潜力。所以，回答你的问题：喜剧是 AI 最难搞定的类型。是的，呃，但其他类型它能更轻松地做。它现在就能写大纲。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: And so I, I, I think whether or not studios want to do it, they, they haven't, um, felt like they can now. Uh, but it, it is, it's right there. Like, it's not in, like, the distant future that it'll be able to do that stuff. And comedy, like, comedy's hard as it to do but comedy is in decline in terms of the productions that are getting done for.
turns.zh: 所以，我、我觉得，无论制片厂想不想这么干，他们现在还……呃，还没觉得自己能这么干。呃，但它就、就在那儿摆着。就是说，AI 能做那些事并不是遥远的未来。而喜剧，喜剧对它来说很难，但喜剧本身正在衰退，就实际做出来的制作量而言。

turns.en: Sure have you experimented at all with ai comedy writing you know just for fun like would you ask it to produce a A Peter-voiced family guy kind of joke?
turns.zh: 当然。你有没有试过用 AI 写喜剧，就是纯为了好玩，比如让它产出一个 Peter 嗓音的 Family Guy 式笑话？

turns.en: That's how I'll make my way back to family guy, I think. I'll pitch as like the AI guy. No, I haven't really done that. My dad does send me a lot of AI-generated content.
turns.zh: 我想那就是我重回 Family Guy 的方式了，我就去自荐当那个'AI guy'。没有，我还真没这么干过。不过我爸确实会发给我很多 AI 生成的内容。

turns.en: Does he, like, send it to you? Oh, yeah. He's like, check out what I just did on ChatGPT.
turns.zh: 他会主动发给你？哦，是的。他会说'看看我刚在 ChatGPT 上做的东西'。

turns.en: Yeah. I mean, like, he's been interested in AI for a long time and, like, and has been saying, he's a business professor and has been saying for years that this is something that they're going to, that AI is going to be able to do. I've always dismissed it, and he was right. But it's, I do kind of, this may be naive, I think, writing... And acting will be among the last categories that AI... But this is the thing. In fiction, in TV and film, we have already been competing for years against the sum of all human creativity produced and distributed for free, algorithmically sorted exactly to your specifications. You can't really scare us with AI compared to this.
turns.zh: 是的。我是说，他对 AI 感兴趣已经很久了，他是一位商学教授，多年来一直在说，这是 AI 迟早能做到的事。我一直不以为然，结果他是对的。不过这……我确实觉得——这可能有点天真——写作……还有表演，会是 AI 最后才能攻克的类别之一。但关键在于：在虚构作品领域，在影视里，我们多年来一直在跟'人类全部创造力的总和'竞争，而这些内容是免费生产和分发的，还被算法精确地按照你的口味排序。跟这个比起来，你真没法用 AI 吓到我们。

turns.en: This is what I always say about journalism, too, because people are like, oh, do you think AI is going to, like, be bad for newspapers or whatever? And I was like, you're talking about an industry that's been buffeted in every direction over the last 20 years.
turns.zh: 关于新闻业我也总是这么说，因为人们会说'哦，你觉得 AI 会不会对报纸之类的不利？'我就说：你谈论的是一个在过去 20 年里被各个方向反复冲击的行业。

turns.en: Yes.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: So, like, possible, but, like, man, if there's one industry that has just taken it on the chin over and over and over again by Google News, by everything else, it's like, at this point, it's like.
turns.zh: 所以，是有可能，但是，天哪，如果真有一个行业被 Google News、被所有其他东西一次又一次地正面硬扛下来，那么到了现在这个地步，就……

turns.en: There isn't... A whole lot.
turns.zh: 也没什么……

turns.en: Left to like. And you talk about AI being cheaper. It is not as cheap as free.
turns.zh: 剩下多少可失去的了。你还说 AI 更便宜，可它再便宜也便宜不过'免费'。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: And like the free content that we all produce for everyone else's consumption all day long. And, you know, we still only have so many consumption hours in our lives.
turns.zh: 还有我们大家整天为别人的消费生产的那些免费内容。而且你知道，我们一辈子能用来消费的时间也就那么多。

turns.en: You know, by the way, every time a new model comes out, one of my tests is I'll have it say like, write 10 tweets in.
turns.zh: 顺便说一句，每次有新模型出来，我的一个测试就是让它：写 10 条推文，用

turns.en: The style of Joe Wiesenthal. And it's never very good.
turns.zh: Joe Wiesenthal 的风格。而且从来都写得不怎么样。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: But.
turns.zh: 不过。

turns.en: You are one of the harder ones, I think, to pin down.
turns.zh: 我觉得你是比较难被模仿到位的那类人之一。

turns.en: But there was one tweet and it said, the 10-year yield doesn't care about your feelings. And frankly, it doesn't care about mine either.
turns.zh: 但有一条推文是这么写的：'10 年期收益率不在乎你的感受。而且坦白说，它也不在乎我的感受。'

turns.en: Oh, no. And I was like, I wouldn't tweet that, but it's.
turns.zh: 哦不。我心想，我可不会发这种推文，但它又……

turns.en: Kind of a good tweet. That's pretty good.
turns.zh: 还挺像一条好推文的。挺不错的。

turns.en: I was like, I kind of like that tweet.
turns.zh: 我就想，我还挺喜欢这条推文的。

turns.en: Wow.
turns.zh: 哇。

turns.en: Yeah. Does it ever say that it doesn't troll?
turns.zh: 是啊。它有没有说过它不'钓鱼'（troll）？

turns.en: It hasn't said that, so it doesn't know me yet.
turns.zh: 它还没说过这个，所以它还不够了解我。

turns.en: Was that scary? They got, they got, they're in the, in the area.
turns.zh: 这吓人吗？他们算是摸到、摸到门道了，就在这附近了。

turns.en: I was like, but it wasn't my voice.
turns.zh: 我就想，可那不是我的语气。

turns.en: So I was like, it wasn't there yet. So you've done a lot with like housing and real estate.
turns.zh: 所以我觉得，它还没到位。那么，你在住房和房地产方面做了很多。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: Have there been a ripple effect from this decline of shoot days in terms of like how you see it manifested quote, the rest of the real economy here?
turns.zh: 拍摄日的这种下滑，有没有产生连锁反应？就是就你看到的、它在'这里其余真实经济'中的体现而言？

turns.en: Yes. I was in City Hall from 2021 to 2024. So during a lot of that decline, during the strike, so I was in City Hall. And I got to see, you know, like working with a lot of small businesses. We say here a lot that Hollywood is not LA and it's not the LA economy. It's like 20% of the economy or something. But it's not a silo.
